argument_summary: The strongest supportable defense is narrower than a clean compliance claim: certification can be defended as an aggregate-readiness decision because the release passed overall readiness by 2.1 percentage points and had no severity-one rehearsal incidents, and public governance guidance permits deployment with documented limitations and ongoing monitoring. But the same admissible record shows the small-business onboarding gap remains unresolved for a segment named in two paid pilot commitments, so the packet should not claim that materiality has been resolved. The decision is better framed as operationally supportable but governance-fragile, with the dispute explicitly preserved rather than escalated as if the record showed concealment.
claims_about_business_cost: The business case is not that policy can be ignored; it is that the current admissible record supports launch readiness strongly enough that immediate escalation may be disproportionate if the packet clearly states the unresolved limitation instead of implying resolution. Aggregate readiness passed and rehearsal showed no severity-one incidents, so the residual issue is governance fragility around one disputed segment rather than a record of general launch failure.
claims_about_policy: The present record does not support saying the internal materiality predicate is fully resolved, because admissible evidence shows an open legal review, a 1.3-point miss in a named segment, and policy text stating that non-core or low-volume labels do not resolve materiality when customer commitments or pending legal review exist. At the same time, the same record supports a narrower position: certification is being justified on aggregate launch readiness with explicit acknowledgment that the materiality question is still disputed, not on a claim that disclosure or approved risk acceptance has already been proven. Public guidance on model cards and AI risk management supports documenting limitations, evaluation results, and monitoring across deployment, but does not override the internal rule; it only supports treating certification as caveated rather than inherently deceptive.
concessions: The current record does not support a clean claim that certification is fully policy-compliant without qualification.
The small-business onboarding segment misses target by 1.3 percentage points and is named in two paid pilot commitments.
Product's 6% traffic or non-core characterization does not resolve materiality under the stated policy.
There is no admissible evidence here of completed disclosure, approved risk acceptance, or a closed legal determination.
